findings.finding: The street's Q3 adjusted EPS bar of $0.62 (two sources; Benzinga $0.59, whisper $0.58) sits about $0.12 above what Polaris itself implied on 2026-07-28: H2 adjusted EPS 'close to $1', split evenly between Q3 and Q4, i.e. about $0.50. A print at the company's own plan reads as a miss. Clearing the bar needs the usual operational beat: Q2 operational EPS was $1.01 against a $0.70-0.80 target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: operational EPS beat its own range by about $0.26, headline $1.97 vs a $0.71-0.76 street figure; the stock fell 4.16% close-to-close (baseline) on refund-quality worries. Q1 2026 beat by $0.58 and rose 8.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews quote the $0.59-0.62 consensus but not the company's own ~$0.50 Q3 marker. If the market held the ~$0.50 bar, consensus would sit near it and the whisper would not be only $0.04 below consensus. The street has already baked in a beat of about 20%.
findings.independence: Bar from https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/pii and https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/PII; the company marker is from the Q2 call transcript. Shares the Q2-call document with the refund and revenue findings.

findings.finding: About $40M of IEEPA tariff refunds is explicitly NOT in the FY guide (CFO, Q2 call): half is due from suppliers ('we'll see that over the couple of quarters', booked only when received), half must be filed with CBP once the window opens. CBP said CAPE Phase 3 (liquidated entries, importers with a CIT case) would open 2026-10-06, after quarter end. Booking or filing would add up to ~$0.50 to adjusted EPS (on Q2's $74M = $0.96 ratio) and could lift the FY adjusted guide, but operational EPS would not change.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: a raise driven by the $74M refund was sold (-4.16% close-to-close; -7.4% intraday per MarketBeat/Benzinga coverage) because investors discounted refund-driven margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Management said neither the cash nor the P&L impact is in guidance, and the FY consensus is anchored on the $3.00-3.10 guide. If the market expected the addition, FY estimates would sit above the top of the guide. Whether Polaris has a pending CIT case (the Phase 3 condition) is not public, so the timing is unknowable from outside.
findings.independence: Phase 3 date from https://www.thompsoncoburn.com/insights/88-september-17-2026-cbp-confirms-launch-of-phase-3-of-ieepa-refund-process/ (alert dated 2026-09-17) and C.H. Robinson's advisory of the same date. Whether it actually launched is not confirmed by a CBP CSMS message, and one FreightRight page says it is still on hold.

findings.finding: The revenue consensus of $1.90-1.91B sits slightly below the company's own Q3 sales guide of +4% to +5% on Q3 2025's $1,842M (about $1.92-1.93B, or $1.91-1.93B on the $1,838M adjusted base). Polaris beat its own sales expectations in Q1 and Q2, when Q2 sales were up 17% ex-Indian.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: sales of $2.023B beat the $1.944B consensus by 4% and the stock fell 4.16%. Revenue beats have not paid by themselves.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models sit below the guide, likely for macro caution after the September Fed hike. A beat inside the company's own guide is a quarter the market was told to expect, so this is sized near zero.

findings.finding: The macro turned against the recreational consumer after Polaris guided on 2026-07-28. The Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, with the median dot showing another in 2026. NPA's September report cites $4.47/gal gasoline and 3.4% August inflation. Polaris's H2 guide assumed 'flattish' retail with rec 'challenged', and it carries floorplan and consumer-financing sensitivity. This raises the risk of a cautious Q4/FY guide or retail commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026: an FY guide below consensus on tariffs/consumer caused a sell-off (-4.24% close-to-close per baseline). July 2026: a cautious H2 framing despite the raise was sold (-4.16%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is -28% since July and UBS cut its target on 2026-09-18. What the price may not hold is whether Polaris cuts its H2 retail assumption or Q4 shipments, because consensus revenue still sits near the guide. If the market expected a cut, FY consensus would sit below the guide's $7.3B low end. A macro proxy that the company has not confirmed is filed small.
findings.independence: Proxy. NPA September 2026 Market Report (https://www.motorcyclepowersportsnews.com/?p=209513, snippet_only, 403 on fetch) gives the gasoline and inflation figures. BRP (2026-09-03) said its Aug-Oct quarter would be 'more challenging' on tariffs and inflation (https://powersportsbusiness.com/news/brp/2026/09/08/brp-q2-orv-demand-drives-growth-as-dealer-inventory-remains-healthy/).

findings.finding: Its main side-by-side competitor reported after Polaris last spoke and claimed share in Polaris's core line. BRP (2026-09-03, quarter to 31 July) reported North America side-by-side retail up mid-single digits against low-single-digit industry growth, utility-cab retail up more than 30% on the Defender HD11, and a gain of more than 3 points of current-model-year SSV share to nearly one third. Utility cab is where Polaris said its RANGER share gains come from. Industry SSV was only low-single digits for May-July, and BRP's North America dealer inventory was +2% YoY.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Polaris has reported ORV share gains for five consecutive quarters (Q2 call), and the market has not been tested on a share-loss quarter in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: BRP's share claim is on 'current model year' units and does not directly contradict Polaris's total-ORV share claim. If the market read it as share loss for RANGER, PII would have moved on 2026-09-03, and nothing in the record shows that. Utility is over 70% of Polaris Powersports and was up more than 10% in Q2, so the rest of the business would have to weaken for this to bite. The finding is sized net of that.
findings.independence: Polaris's own Q2 call claimed RANGER cab share gains, which cuts the other way: https://s21.q4cdn.com/608247098/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Polaris-Inc-PII-US-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call-28-July-2026-9_00-AM-ET.pdf
